messages:
Maria (Support): Hey team — escalated from ACME. Aparna reports the /v1/rerank call failing with a token/char limit error when they send large queries + ~300 docs. Error payload: `400 {\"error\":{\"code\":\"request_too_large\",\"message\":\"request exceeds token/char limits\"}}`. They say it used to return scores for smaller batches. Can someone help repro and advise what we should tell them?

Aparna (ACME): hi! reproducer attached. We were trying to rerank search results where query is long (user query + context ~8k chars) and the docs array had ~300 short docs (avg 600 chars). We get the 400 and nothing else. No per-doc info. How should we format/limit? Is there an automatic truncation? We can't change UX much on our side.

Maria (Support): Thanks Aparna. Sharing the curl we used from the customer:

```
curl https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "model": "r-rerank-1",
    "query": "<very long search query ~8000 chars>",
    "documents": [{"id":"d1","text":"<~600 chars>"}, ..., {"id":"d300","text":"<~600 chars>"}],
    "top_k": 10
  }'
```

ops-bot: Incoming rate-limit metadata: project=acme, region=us-west-2, plan=standard. No quota hit recorded.

Josh (Eng-ML): I can repro locally with a script. Behavior: we reject with 400 when the total estimated tokens (query + sum(tokens(doc.text))) exceed 32768 tokens for that model variant. Customer-facing message is generic — we should improve it. For rerank, we actually compute token counts using the model tokenizer, but we currently only return a single `request_too_large` string.

Josh (Eng-ML): Repro script (pseudo):
```
# python-ish
q = 'x' * 8000
docs = ['y'*600]*300
resp = client.rerank(model='r-rerank-1', query=q, documents=[{'text':d} for d in docs])
print(resp.status_code, resp.json())
```
Result: 400 + message above. If I reduce docs to 50 it succeeds. If I truncate query to 2000 chars it succeeds. So the limit behaves as expected.

Maria (Support): Can we provide the customer with exact numbers (max tokens, recommended max docs, how to calculate) and a helpful error message to land in the meantime?

Sasha (Product): We should also consider whether we can change the API error to be actionable: include fields like `limit_type: tokens|docs|chars`, `limit_value`, `actual_value`, and optionally `offending_doc_index` if a single doc is too long. Product asks for a quick mitigation (docs + support message) and a follow-up to change API shape.

Anika (Docs): I'll draft a support doc and snippet. Proposed support reply:
- Explain current hard limit (r-rerank-1: 32,768 tokens aggregate).
- Suggest strategies: truncate query to 2k chars, batch rerank into chunks of <= 100 docs, or send only doc summaries.
- Provide utility snippet (node/python) to compute tokens before call and pre-split docs.

Aparna (ACME): Would prefer server-side auto-truncate so our UX isn't impacted. Also need an error code we can detect to show a helpful message in-app. Right now it shows "Something went wrong" to users.

Josh (Eng-ML): Server auto-truncate for rerank is risky — truncating docs can change scores unpredictably. But we can: 1) return structured error with details (recommended), 2) provide a best-effort `truncated=true` mode behind a flag that truncates docs and returns a warning. Both are doable.

Sasha (Product): Prioritize structured error first (fast). Truncation flag is medium-term. Also include a per-model docs table for limits.

Josh (Eng-ML): Implementation notes: we already compute tokens per document. We can change the error payload like: `400 {\"error\":{\"code\":\"rerank_request_too_large\",\"message\":\"request exceeds token limit\",\"details\":{\"limit_tokens\":32768,\"actual_tokens\":42300,\"top_offenders\":[{\"index\":12,\"tokens\":12000},{\"index\":7,\"tokens\":9800}]}}}`. That will let ACME detect and surface UX. I'll open an internal PR to include top_offenders and limit_type.

Anika (Docs): I'll update the doc page with sample error and recommended client-side code. Draft snippet for JavaScript to estimate tokens using our tokenizer cli:```js
// pseudo
const tokens = tokenizer.countTokens(query) + docs.reduce((s,d)=>s+tokenizer.countTokens(d.text),0);
if (tokens > 32768) throw new Error('split into smaller batches');
```
Also include example curl that returns the improved JSON error.

Maria (Support): For now, what should I tell ACME?

Josh (Eng-ML): Tell them: 1) current aggregate token limit is 32,768 for r-rerank-1 (includes query + all docs). 2) If you hit this, split your rerank into batches of <=100 docs or shorten the query. 3) We're rolling out a change that will return a structured error with `top_offenders` within 48h. 4) We will evaluate an opt-in `truncated=true` server behavior for risky autop-trimming.

Aparna (ACME): Ok thanks — can you also confirm whether `documents[].text` char count vs token count mapping you use (we're in JS so would like a helper lib).

Anika (Docs): I'll publish a small JS helper in docs and a gist. It will include an approximate chars->tokens heuristic (avg 4 chars per token) plus links to exact tokenizer binaries for accurate counts.

Sasha (Product): Ticket: PROD-1328 created to track error shape change + docs + customer communication. Assign to Josh for implementation and Anika for docs. Engineering ETA: 48h for error shape change (non-breaking: adds fields), 2 weeks for truncation opt-in.

ops-bot: Created ticket PROD-1328 (https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/PROD-1328) assigned to Josh.

Josh (Eng-ML): I'll push a tiny API patch later today to return `rerank_request_too_large` with `details.top_offenders` for the next deploy. I'll include a quick unit test showing detection when a single doc > 12k tokens.

Maria (Support): Awesome. I'll reply to ACME now with the interim guidance and link to this thread + the upcoming docs. Thanks everyone! :heart:

Aparna (ACME): Thanks all — appreciate the quick turnaround.

Josh (Eng-ML): follow-up note: we should also consider a separate hard cap on number of docs (e.g., 1000) to prevent OOMs. I'll add that to the ticket.

Sasha (Product): Good call. Add limit_type "docs_count" to the error payload as well.

Anika (Docs): Will add an FAQ entry: 'Why did my rerank fail with request_too_large?' with examples and migration steps.
